paper.title: A Theoretical Model for Grit in Pursuing Ambitious Ends

settings.name_in_paper: Improving two-armed bandit with cost to strive and gamma-comfort constraint (competitive ratio)
unmapped: Improving bandit: arm rewards are deterministic functions of the number of times (possibly fractional) the arm has been played
Stable arm f1(t)=1; striving arm f2(t)=-1 for t<theta and t-theta afterwards, with unknown threshold theta (worst-case over theta)
Objective is the competitive ratio ALG/OPT (worst case over theta), not additive regret
Comfort constraint: accrued reward at every time t must be at least gamma*t; the learner knows gamma
settings.definition_quote: f_1(t) = 1 \, \forall \, t and f_2(t) = -1 for t < \theta, t-\theta for t \ge \theta ... We say an agent wants to be $\gamma$-comfortable if at any time $t > 0\,,$ they need their net reward to be at least $\gamma \cdot t\,.$

algorithms.name: Minimally accumulating switch-point strategy for gamma-comfortable agent

symbols.gamma_c: comfort level: required minimum average accrued reward, in [0,1)

conditions: two arms: f1(t)=1, f2(t)=-1 for t<theta and t-theta for t>=theta (alpha=1)
accrued reward must be at least gamma*t at all times
tuning: alternate alpha_gamma=(gamma+1)/2 time on f1 and 1-alpha_gamma on f2, switching permanently to f1 at time T - gamma/2 - sqrt(gamma^2+4T(2-gamma))/2

source.label: lemma:gamma-comfort
source.quote: Suppose an agent who wants to be $\gamma$-comfortable plays $f_1$ for $\alpha_\gamma$ time followed by $f_2$ for $1-\alpha_\gamma$ time before reverting back to $f_1\,$ and continuing the process. Then, the agent wanting to maximize their competitive ratio subject to the constraint of the average reward always being at least $\gamma$ will switch after absolute time $T - \frac{\gamma}{2} - \frac12 \sqrt{\gamma^2 + 4T(2-\gamma)}$, achieving competitive ratio $\gamma + \frac{\gamma(1-\gamma)}{2T} + \frac{(1-\gamma) \sqrt{\gamma^2 - 4T (2 - \gamma)}}{2T}$.

results.notes: Statement has sqrt(gamma^2 - 4T(2-gamma)), which would be imaginary; the appendix proof derives sqrt(gamma^2 + 4T(2-gamma)), which is recorded here. Remark 3.10 (CR approx 0.55 at T=150, gamma=0.5) agrees with the + version. A competitive ratio is a guarantee ALG/OPT >= g; 'upper' side is used for an achievability guarantee. Deterministic model, so probability set to almost_sure.
